_comment: 🧩️ This subset's contribution to the repository test platform: the mutation oracle and vocabulary for stdio.obj 3.0/✳️any, distinct from the shared `tobj` id already registered under `obj-mesh` in ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json (that entry is surveyed for mesh creation, not for this subset's 22-kind mutation vocabulary — reusing it here would fail the contract with oracle-capability-mismatch).

oracles.rationale: OBJ has no reference WRITER in the Rust ecosystem — it is a plain-text grammar — so this subset's oracle applies every declared mutation kind by direct grammar manipulation (mirroring the same precedent the shared `tobj` mesh-creation oracle already uses) and `tobj` serves as the independent reader every oracle and subject result is projected through before comparison. `tobj` alone is not enough to judge this vocabulary: it triangulates, re-indexes per `o`/`g` model and drops every row no face references, so 14 of the 22 declared kinds move nothing in its reading at all. The projection therefore composes that `tobj` mesh reading with this module's own `oracle_document_projection` -- declared `v`/`vt`/`vn` row counts and per-component extent, the `mtllib` reference, the `g`/`o` membership spans, the `usemtl`/`s` run starts and the retained comment lines -- and the case asserts in role that every kind but `no-mutation` actually moves it. That document half is read by this module's independent grammar parser, which never touches the subject's `decode_obj`, so it stays a second reader rather than a self-comparison.

comparisonProfiles.description: Wavefront OBJ documents compared by the `tobj` triangle mesh (vertex set, face topology, counts) AND by the document surface a mesh reader cannot see: declared v/vt/vn row counts with their per-component extent and totals, the mtllib reference, the g/o membership spans, the usemtl/s run starts and the retained comment lines. Unlike the shared semantic-mesh-v1 profile, none of those are writer freedom here -- ObjMutation's set-mtllib/set-usemtl/set-smoothing-groups/set-unknown-statements and the four name-keyed g/o kinds mutate exactly that surface, so ignoring it would leave 14 of the 22 declared kinds unobservable. Only byte length and decimal precision remain producer freedom; per-component extents and totals are compared under the mesh tolerance so the two producers' differing decimal formatting never registers as a divergence.
